So 10^100 S = sum_{m>=1} d(m) 10^{100-m}. Integer part: sum_{m=1}^{100} d(m) 10^{100-m} plus fractional part sum_{m>101...}. Careful: carries. Actually 10^100 S = N + f where N = sum_{m=1}^{100} d(m)10^{100-m} (an integer), f = sum_{m>100} d(m)10^{100-m} <1? Let's check f = sum_{j>=1} d(100+j) 10^{-j}. d grows slowly but d(100+j) can exceed 10... f = 0.1*d(101) + 0.01*d(102)+... d(101)=2, so 0.2 + ... d(102)=8 -> 0.08, d(103)=2 ->0.002, d(104)=8->0.0008,... Sum roughly 0.2+0.08+0.002+... Total likely less than 1. Indeed sum d(100+j)10^{-j} — average d ~ ln(n)~5, so ~5/9*0.1... but first term dominates: 0.2+0.08+0.002+0.0008+0.00012(d(105)=8)... total ~0.283. Less than 1. Good.

So floor = N = sum_{m=1}^{100} d(m) 10^{100-m}. Mod 1000: only terms with 100-m <= 2, i.e., m=98,99,100: d(98)*100 + d(99)*10 + d(100)*1.

d(98)=98=2*7^2 -> 6. d(99)=9*11=3^2*11 -> 6. d(100)=2^2*5^2 -> 9.
6*100+6*10+9 = 600+60+9=669. Mod 1000 = 669.
